title: Ellington and Hines on the radio; black-key piano; leaving school in seventh grade
summary: He listened to Ellington and Earl Hines, tried piano on the black keys in a trio, and left school to sell papers and shine shoes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: So, I still kept my ears glued to the radio, listening to Duke Ellington, Earl 'Father' Hines. Those two people were idols, musically, you know musically -- that was all you could hear.

I had made up my mind I was going to be a musician, but how? -- because I didn't have no musical learning. I didn't learn in school, they didn't have nothing to play. So I started foolin' around with the piano. I only could play in all the black keys. But that was all right, we got by. We had a little trio called Wynken, Blynken and Nod.
I left school in the 7th grade. I couldn't afford to go to a school no more. Hit the streets. I was always sellin' papers, shinin' shoes from as long as I can remember.
